questions.q: (a) Describe the life cycle of a star much more massive than the Sun [4]. (b) Compare the orbit of a comet with that of a planet [2]. (c) State what a blue star tells us about its surface temperature [1].
questions.a: (a) nebula (1); main sequence (1); red supergiant (1); supernova then neutron star or black hole (1); (b) comet orbit very elliptical, planet nearly circular (1); comet speed varies greatly, fastest near the Sun (1); (c) very hot (1)
questions.model: Teacher writes (a) step 1: 'A nebula of gas and dust collapses under gravity.'

questions.q: Explain why a comet travels fastest when closest to the Sun.
questions.a: Gravitational force strongest close to the Sun (1); comet accelerates as it falls in (1); gravitational potential energy converted to kinetic energy (1)

questions.q: A 70 kg person's weight on Mars (g = 3.7 N/kg)?
A planet orbits at 1.5 × 10¹¹ m with a period of 3.2 × 10⁷ s. Orbital speed?
Why is g on the Moon smaller than on Earth?
questions.a: The Moon has much less mass

questions.q: What will the Sun become at the end of its life?
questions.a: A white dwarf (after a red giant)
